$comment: Validation matrix for the Tizen device lane and visual baselines.
This file deliberately does NOT restate the target-framework contract. That lives in
tizenFxApiLevel, referencePack) and is the single source of truth. Duplicating it here
is how the two drift. Tests read the target contract via RepositoryBaselines and the
'alsoValidTargets' below lists platform versions the workload may additionally accept.
Only entries with confirmed=true participate in release gating; the rest are exercised
opportunistically and reported, because they have not been verified against real Samsung

emulator.notes: Provisioned on the self-hosted runner by eng/validation/scripts/tizen-device-lane.sh. Never pinned to a named machine or account in this repository.
TV emulator images come from Tizen Studio's TV extension; see docs/validation/device-lane.md.

$comment: Evaluated on the hosted lane against restored dependency graphs (obj/project.assets.json).
These catch transitive resolutions that would only fail at runtime on a device.

bannedResolutions.reason: Tizen.UIExtensions still carries .NET 6-era Microsoft.Maui.Graphics dependencies (eng/baselines.json > target.notes). Those resolve into the net11.0-tizen11.0 graph and surface as missing-type failures on device rather than as build errors. Tizen.UIExtensions must be republished without them.
$expectedStatusComment: 'known-violation' means the banned resolution is currently PRESENT in the published
package and is a tracked external prerequisite (eng/baselines.json > target.notes:
Tizen.UIExtensions must be republished to drop its .NET 6-era Graphics dependencies).
The tripwire test asserts reality matches this field in BOTH directions, so when
Samsung republishes, CI fails and tells us to flip it to 'clean' and make the rule

$comment: Baseline images are addressed by profile/apiLevel/theme/density so that a single control
can hold several legitimately different renderings without ambiguity.
